input.quote: NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL, RELIANCE OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES OR LOST OR IMPUTED PROFITS OR ROYALTIES OR COST OF PROCUREMENT OF SUBSTITUTE GOODS OR SERVICES
input.rationale: Section 15.11 (p0833) is the only limitation-of-liability provision: it contains a mutual indirect/consequential damages waiver (which already meets that element) but no aggregate monetary cap and no carve-out architecture. Article 12 (indemnification), the 13.6 disclaimer and 14.4.2 (which only channels SFJ's termination damages into the Section 14.2 payments) add no cap, and document-wide searches for \"aggregate liability\" and \"shall not exceed\" return nothing responsive, so both Parties' direct liability is unlimited and the rule fails. We cure at preferred with two surgical operations: a single mutual cap sentence at the greater of the fees paid or payable by PB under this Agreement in the twelve months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000 (Agreement-wide base, not confined to Article 6, and the floor keeps the cap meaningful given that PB's payments are event-driven), carrying the seven uncapped carve-outs; and an in-place extension of the retained savings sentence making it mutual, so that neither Party's payment obligations — including SFJ's Article 4 Development Cost funding and the Section 14.2 amounts — are \"damages\" subject to the cap. Confidentiality is tied to \"this Agreement\" to avoid any dangling cross-reference; every other word of 15.11 survives verbatim.

proposal.summary: Mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable by PB under the Agreement and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped carve-outs for indemnities, confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and a mutual confirmation that payment obligations are not capped damages
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 15.11 waives indirect damages but leaves both Parties' direct liability entirely uncapped, so we have added a mutual cap at the greater of the fees paid or payable by PB under this Agreement in the twelve months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000. Indemnification, confidentiality, data protection and security, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and we have made the savings sentence mutual so that neither Party's payment obligations (including SFJ's Article 4 funding) are "damages" subject to the cap.

ops.text: Except for each Party's indemnification obligations under Article 12, each Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations under this Agreement, each Party's breach of its data protection or security obligations, each Party's gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud, and each Party's infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement will not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by PB under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and (b) One Million U.S. Dollars ($1,000,000).

ops.oldText: FOR THE AVOIDANCE OF DOUBT, THIS SECTION 15.11 IS NOT MEANT TO LIMIT PB'S OBLIGATION TO PAY SFJ THE AMOUNTS SET FORTH IN ARTICLE 6 OR SECTION 14.2.
ops.newText: FOR THE AVOIDANCE OF DOUBT, THIS SECTION 15.11 IS NOT MEANT TO LIMIT PB'S OBLIGATION TO PAY SFJ THE AMOUNTS SET FORTH IN ARTICLE 6 OR SECTION 14.2; NEITHER PARTY'S PAYMENT OBLIGATIONS UNDER THIS AGREEMENT ARE "DAMAGES" SUBJECT TO ANY CAP.
